newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN CO. BUYS BACK, CANCELS SHARES.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN CO. BUYS BACK, CANCELS SHARES.

text.p: Belgian brewer Interbrew NV has sold 43,141 shares, or 35.24 percent, of Societe Commerciale de Brasserie SA (Co.Br.Ha), according to a notice published in Belgian newspapers.
The shares were bought by Co.Br.Ha at 10,000 Belgian francs each, or a total 431.4 million Belgian francs.

Co.Br.Ha, which is 47.12 percent controlled by Belgian privately-held companies Gefi and Finabra, said it would extend the offer to other minority shareholders following an extraordinary general shareholders meeting on February 21.

At least 35.24 percent of the acquired shares would be cancelled, Co.Br.Ha said. Any additional shares acquired, up to a maximum 10 percent, would be held as treasury stock and could be replaced in the market.
"These acquisitions will be realised on the stock exchange over a proposed period of three months," Co.Br.Ha said.
"The treasury stock...which is not cancelled can be resold on the bourse to stimulate the market in such a way that the quotation of the shares can be maintained," it added.
